title: Request Courier Sentinel and Backpressure Tamer
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Add a lightweight SDK middleware (Courier Sentinel) and associated tracing hooks to detect request fanout, annotate traces with backpressure signals, and provide low-overhead sampling hints for downstream services. The goal is to reduce undiagnosed latency spikes from uncontrolled fanout and to make backpressure visible in the Redwood Console latency/error dashboards. This ticket covers design, implementation across Node/Python SDKs, tests, benchmarks, and a canary rollout plan.
design_decisions: 1) Use a compact single header 'x-rw-courier' for propagation to minimize header bloat. 2) Attach a small JSON-safe sentinel payload with fields: hop_id, fanout_count_hint, backpressure_flag, sample_hint. 3) Implement middleware that increments fanout_count_hint on fork points and sets backpressure_flag when queue depth or rate limiter returns 429/503. 4) Keep default sampling unchanged; use sample_hint only as a soft suggestion to downstream agents. 5) Provide opt-out via SDK config and respect existing enterprise header filtering rules.
tradeoffs: - Header minimalism vs. extensibility: chosen compact header reduces network overhead but requires careful versioning for added fields. - Soft sampling hint avoids hard coupling with downstream sampling policies but may be ignored by some clients. - Implementing in multiple SDKs increases surface area but is necessary for end-to-end visibility.

acceptance_criteria: Courier header is emitted by Node and Python SDKs in opt-in mode
Propagation preserves hop_id and fanout_count_hint across async boundaries
Observed overhead <= 2ms median and p95 < 6ms in microbench on typical request path
Console surface shows new backpressure metric and a trace annotation for fanout_count_hint
End-to-end test demonstrating backpressure_flag set when downstream returns 429
Security review completed and header documented in privacy guide
qa_plan: Unit tests for header parsing/serialization, integration tests against local observability stack (Jaeger-compatible traces + logs), load test with synthetic fanout to validate telemetry scales, and fuzzing to validate header resilience against malformed values.
rollout_plan: 1) Feature gated behind account opt-in flag in Console. 2) Enable for internal Redwood orgs and run 48h smoke + perf. 3) Canary for 5% of traffic for customers who opt in (monitor error/latency deltas). 4) Gradual ramp with rollback criteria defined (increase in p99 latency > 5% or error rate > 0.5%).
benchmarks: Microbench: Node SDK middleware adds median 1.2ms and p95 4.8ms on dev GPU-backed environment. Python SDK median 1.6ms and p95 5.2ms. End-to-end with fanout to 10 children: trace tag propagation maintained and Console dashboard showed aggregated fanout_count histogram without noticeable ingestion increase (<3% telemetry volume delta).
open_questions: 1) Should sample_hint values be numeric weights or categorical low/med/high? 2) Best default for fanout_count_hint when exact fanout is unknown (0 vs 1)? 3) Backpressure_flag semantics across retries - should retries reset flag?
